models.name: discussion_board_configurations
models.description:
System-wide configuration settings and feature flags controlling platform behavior.

Manages customizable platform parameters that determine feature availability, performance limits, moderation thresholds, and system behavior. These configurations are independently managed by administrators through direct UI or API interactions, allowing dynamic control of platform functionality without code deployments.

Each configuration setting is a key-value pair that can be toggled, modified, or deactivated. Configurations affect the entire platform and are cached for performance. Changes take effect immediately across all users and sessions.

Examples include: comment character limits, attachment size restrictions, posting frequency caps, moderation automation thresholds, and feature flags for experimental functionality.

plainFields.name: key
plainFields.description: Unique configuration identifier (e.g., "comment_max_length", "attachment_file_size_limit"). Must be unique across all configurations.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Configuration value stored as string for flexibility. Can represent boolean ("true"/"false"), numeric ("100"), or string values ("default").

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description explaining the purpose and usage of this configuration setting.

plainFields.name: is_enabled
plainFields.description: Whether this configuration is currently active and applied to the system. When false, system falls back to default behavior.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration was initially created and added to the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration was last modified by an administrator.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration was soft-deleted. NULL indicates active configuration. Used for audit trails and potential recovery.

models.name: discussion_board_channels
models.description:
Data channels for organizing content categories such as Economics, Politics, and Society.

Defines hierarchical and thematic categories that organize all user-generated content on the platform. Each channel represents a distinct topic area where citizens can post articles, engage in discussions, and find relevant content. Channels serve as the primary organizational structure for content discovery and navigation.

Channels are created and managed by moderators with appropriate permissions. Citizens can browse and search content by channel, but cannot create or delete channels. Each article belongs to exactly one channel, and the channel metadata (name, description) remains consistent even if the content within changes.

Soft deletion is supported to maintain audit trails while allowing for channel deactivation or reorganization.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Unique display name of the channel (e.g., "Economics", "Politics", "Society"). Used for URL routing and category selection.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description explaining what topics this channel covers, any specific rules, and target audience. Provides context for users browsing available channels.

plainFields.name: visibility_flag
plainFields.description: Determines whether the channel is visible to citizens. True = visible in listings and search results. False = hidden from general browsing (but existing content remains accessible).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the channel was created. Immutable and used for audit trails and chronological sorting.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the channel's name or description was last modified. Updated when moderators edit channel metadata.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. When set, the channel is considered archived and hidden from all user interfaces. Used for content moderation without permanent data loss.

models.name: discussion_board_attachments
models.description:
Metadata for media attachments including file type, size, and upload timestamp.

Stores technical information about files uploaded by users to associate with posts, articles, or other content entities. Each attachment is linked to a parent content item and contains only metadata information, not the actual file content which is stored separately in object storage.

Attachment records track file characteristics (MIME type, size) and timing for operational, billing, and compliance purposes. The actual file data resides in external object storage systems referenced by storage paths.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_posts_id
foreignFields.description: Parent post that this attachment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_posts.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_articles_id
foreignFields.description: Parent article that this attachment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comments_id
foreignFields.description: Parent comment that this attachment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the uploaded file (e.g., image/jpeg, application/pdf). Used for content type validation and client rendering.

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: Size of the uploaded file in bytes. Used for storage quota calculation and upload validation against system limits.

plainFields.name: file_name
plainFields.description: Original filename of the uploaded file. Preserved for user reference and download purposes.

plainFields.name: storage_path
plainFields.description: Path to the actual file in the external object storage system. Used to retrieve the file content from CDN or storage service.

plainFields.name: file_hash
plainFields.description: SHA-256 hash of the uploaded file content. Used for integrity verification and duplicate detection across uploads.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment record was created. Immutable record of upload time for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment record was last updated. Used for tracking metadata changes (e.g., renaming).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment was logically deleted (soft delete). Null if still active. Used for compliance and recovery workflows.

models.name: discussion_board_moderation_logs
models.description:
Immutable audit trail of all moderation actions taken on the platform.

Stores a complete historical record of moderator decisions including deletions, warnings, suspensions, and other enforcement actions. This table serves as the primary compliance mechanism for regulatory requirements, providing an unalterable log of all content modifications and user sanctions.

Each audit entry records which moderator performed the action, what content or user was targeted, the specific action taken, the reason provided, and the exact timestamp. The table uses soft delete to maintain audit integrity while allowing for system cleanup of obsolete records.

All entries are timestamped at creation and cannot be modified after logging - even if the target content is later restored or deleted, the audit trail remains intact for forensic review.

foreignFields.name: moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator who performed the action. {@link discussion_board_moderator.id}.

foreignFields.name: target_id
foreignFields.description: Unique identifier of the content or user targeted by the moderation action. This may reference a post, comment, user account, or other entity depending on the action type. {@link discussion_board_posts.id} or {@link discussion_board_comments.id} or {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of moderation action performed. Valid values: 'delete', 'warn', 'suspend', 'ban', 'unhide', 'approve'.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Detailed reason for the moderation action, including policy violation details and moderator justification.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderation action was logged. The immutable point-in-time when this audit record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to this audit record, typically used if metadata is corrected after initial logging.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp for audit record lifecycle management in compliance with data retention policies.

models.name: discussion_board_posts
models.description:
Persistent records of all citizen-authored posts, including title, content, and timestamp.

Stores user-generated content created by citizens on the discussion board platform. Each post represents a complete message with title and body text, linked to a specific author and category channel. Posts are the primary content entities that users create, browse, search, and interact with.

Posts remain accessible even if their associated channel is modified, ensuring content persistency. Authors can edit their own posts, and posts may be hidden or deleted based on moderation actions, which are tracked separately in the Moderation component.

This table supports comprehensive search and filtering across all posts regardless of channel context, enabling users to find content by author, keyword, date, or other criteria independently.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen who authored this post. {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_channel_id
foreignFields.description: The content channel where this post is published. {@link discussion_board_channels.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: The subject or heading of the post. Must be concise and descriptive, typically limited to 150 characters.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: The main content body of the post. Contains the full text of the user's message without formatting.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the post was initially created. Used for ordering and chronological display.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the post was last modified. Updated whenever the user edits the title or body content.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the post was soft-deleted. If null, the post is active. Enables content recovery and moderation audit trails.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current publication status of the post. Valid values: draft, pending, published, hidden. Used to enforce workflow control and moderation decisions. Post visibility and accessibility are determined by status rather than deletion. This field separates workflow state from soft-deletion mechanism.

models.name: discussion_board_authentication_logs
models.description:
Tracks authentication sessions and login events for security auditing.

Records every successful and failed authentication attempt by citizens and moderators, providing critical security audit trails for compliance and forensic analysis. Each entry links to an authenticated actor (citizen or moderator) and captures connection context including IP address, requested URL, and referrer information.

This table is append-only for audit integrity and supports soft deletion only for compliance archival purposes. It does not store authentication credentials but references the primary actor entities in the Actors component.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: References the citizen entity if the login was performed by a citizen. {@link discussion_board_citizen.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: References the moderator entity if the login was performed by a moderator. {@link discussion_board_moderator.id}.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Indicates the actor type that performed this authentication: 'citizen' or 'moderator'. Used for polymorphic relationship with actor_id fields.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: The IP address from which the authentication attempt originated.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: The URL the user was accessing when authentication occurred. Should include full path.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: The previous webpage URL from which the user navigated to this authentication endpoint.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this authentication event was recorded.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this authentication event was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this authentication record was soft-deleted for archival purposes. Null indicates the record is active.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this authentication session expired. Null indicates the session is still active or session expiration isn't applicable.

models.name: discussion_board_users
models.description:
Storage system for user email addresses and hashed credentials for secure authentication.

Contains the core identity information for citizens who register and authenticate to use the discussion board platform.
Each record represents a unique user account with an email address and securely hashed password.

This table is the foundation of user authentication across the entire system, referenced by session tables in the Actors component.
Email addresses are enforced as unique to prevent duplicate registrations.

Soft delete support is provided through deleted_at field to maintain audit trails while allowing account removal.
All authentication logic and user session management occur through this entity.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: User's unique email address for authentication and communication. Must be globally unique across the platform.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: BCrypt-hashed password for secure authentication. Never stores plaintext passwords.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was last updated (e.g., password change).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was soft-deleted. Null indicates active account.

models.name: discussion_board_archives
models.description:
Historical archive of deleted or hidden content for compliance and audit requirements.

Stores immutable snapshots of content (posts, comments, attachments) after they have been removed or hidden by moderators. Each archive record captures the complete state of an entity at the moment of deletion, preserving data for legal compliance, moderation review, and historical analysis.

Archives are automatically created by the system following moderation actions (hide, delete) and are only accessible to moderators and auditors. This table is strictly read-only from a user perspective and serves solely as a regulatory audit trail.

Content type is indicated by the content_type field, which references the original entity's table (posts, comments, attachment_images, attachment_files). The content_id field links to the original entity's primary key before deletion.

Entries in this table are append-only, never modified or deleted once created, ensuring integrity of the audit trail.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_posts_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the archived post. {@link discussion_board_posts.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comments_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the archived comment. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_attachment_images_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the archived image attachment. {@link discussion_board_attachment_images.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_attachment_files_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the archived file attachment. {@link discussion_board_attachment_files.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_moderation_actions_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the moderation action that triggered this archive. {@link discussion_board_moderation_actions.id}.

plainFields.name: content_type
plainFields.description: Type of archived content ("post", "comment", "image", "file"). Used to determine which foreign key field contains the reference.

plainFields.name: content_id
plainFields.description: The original entity's ID before deletion (as stored in the original table). Used along with content_type to reconstruct context.

plainFields.name: content_data
plainFields.description: JSON-encoded string containing the complete state of the archived content at the time of deletion, including all fields.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this archive record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this archive record was last updated (typically only when metadata is added).

plainFields.name: archived_by
plainFields.description: The username or identifier of the moderator who triggered the archive action, if available.

plainFields.name: archived_at
plainFields.description: The exact timestamp when the original content was removed or hidden by moderation action.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason provided by the moderator for archiving this content, extracted from the moderation action.

plainFields.name: archive_reason_code
plainFields.description: Standardized code representing the reason for archiving, mapped from moderation action reason (e.g., "abuse", "spam", "inappropriate", "copyright").

models.name: discussion_board_activity_logs
models.description:
Tracks user behavior and activity patterns for rate-limiting enforcement and platform usage monitoring.

Records all significant user actions that may trigger rate-limiting mechanisms, such as frequent post creation, comment submissions, or report submissions. This log is used by the platform's operational systems to detect abusive behavior patterns and enforce usage policies.

Each record captures the actor (citizen or moderator) who performed the action, the type of activity, the timestamp, and an optional context field for additional details.

This table is append-only for audit purposes and supports soft deletion for compliance with data retention requirements.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen who performed the activity. {@link discussion_board_citizen.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: The moderator who performed the activity. {@link discussion_board_moderator.id}.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of user activity being logged. Examples: 'post_creation', 'comment_submission', 'report_submission', 'upload_attempt', 'login_failed'.

plainFields.name: context
plainFields.description: Optional context information about the activity, such as specific content IDs, error codes, or additional metadata.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the activity was recorded.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for soft deletion, enabling audit trail preservation while allowing content moderation.

models.name: discussion_board_status_logs
models.description:
System status recordings including uptime, maintenance windows, and error events.

Tracks operational health and diagnostic events of the discussion board platform. These are system-generated records used for monitoring, incident analysis, and maintenance tracking. Each entry captures the state of the system at a specific moment with detailed context.

These logs are append-only and immutable - once recorded, status entries are never modified or deleted. They provide the foundation for system reliability reporting and operational audits.

Events are categorized by type (uptime, maintenance, error) and include a human-readable message and technical context for troubleshooting.

plainFields.name: status_type
plainFields.description: Category of the system status event. Valid values: "uptime", "maintenance", "error". Indicates the nature of the system event being logged.

plainFields.name: message
plainFields.description: Human-readable description of the system status event. Provides brief context about what occurred, such as "System restarted after update" or "Database connection timeout".

plainFields.name: context
plainFields.description: JSON-formatted technical details about the system event. Contains structured data for automated analysis, such as error codes, stack traces, affected services, or metrics. May include system environment info, server identifiers, or request IDs.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this system status event was recorded. Indicates the exact moment the system captured this status change or event.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this record was last modified in the database. For system logs, this is typically the same as created_at since these records are immutable, but maintained for consistency with database patterns.

models.name: discussion_board_thumbnails
models.description:
Metadata for automatically generated image thumbnails used in display previews.

Contains resized versions of uploaded images optimized for quick loading in listings and feeds. Thumbnails are automatically created when an image attachment is uploaded and are deleted when the source attachment is removed. This table enables faster UI rendering by serving pre-scaled images instead of processing original uploads on-demand.

Each thumbnail record is uniquely linked to a single image attachment through a foreign key relationship and cannot exist independently. No direct user interaction occurs with thumbnail records - they are managed entirely by the system.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_attachment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the source image attachment that generated this thumbnail. {@link discussion_board_attachments.id}.

plainFields.name: width
plainFields.description: Width of the thumbnail image in pixels. Standardized dimensions for UI display consistency.

plainFields.name: height
plainFields.description: Height of the thumbnail image in pixels. Standardized dimensions for UI display consistency.

plainFields.name: file_path
plainFields.description: Absolute path or URL to the thumbnail file in the content delivery network (CDN).

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the thumbnail image (e.g., 'image/jpeg', 'image/png'). Must match the source file format.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the thumbnail was generated and stored in the system. Follows system-wide temporal field pattern.

models.name: discussion_board_citizen
models.description:
Stores profile information and authentication details for regular users of the discussion board.

Represents citizens who can register, create posts, submit comments, and upload attachments. Each citizen has a unique email and encrypted password for secure authentication. This entity is linked to their active sessions via the citizen_sessions table.

Citizens are primary actors - they independently manage their account, view their posted content, and interact with other users. Soft deletion is supported to maintain audit trails during account deactivation or moderation actions.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address for authentication and notification. Must be validated and verified.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Securely hashed password using Argon2 or bcrypt. Never stored in plain text.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the citizen account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to citizen profile or authentication data.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp; if set, account is deactivated but preserved for audit.

models.name: discussion_board_citizen_sessions
models.description:
Tracks authentication sessions for discussion board citizens, including session tokens and expiration.

Each session represents a user's active connection to the application. Sessions are automatically created upon successful authentication and invalidated upon logout or expiration. This table supports security auditing by tracking IP addresses, connection URLs, and referrer information for each session.

Sessions are managed by authentication flows and do not require direct user interaction. They provide critical audit trails for investigating suspicious activity and verifying user identity attribution.

foreignFields.name: citizen_id
foreignFields.description: Citizen's {@link discussion_board_citizen.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the session was initiated.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL of the connection that established this session.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that led the user to initiate this session.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session expires or is invalidated. Null indicates session is still active.

models.name: discussion_board_moderator
models.description:
Privileged account information for moderators who manage content and user reports.

Stores credentials and authentication details for users with elevated permissions to review, edit, or remove content.
This table exists independently of the main user table to provide specialized access controls for moderation roles.
Each moderator account has unique authentication credentials and cannot be a regular citizen account.
Soft deletion is supported to maintain audit trails while allowing temporary deactivation of moderator privileges.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the primary user account in the Systematic component. {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for authentication and communication. Must be distinct from citizen accounts.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for secure authentication. Never store plain text passwords.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderator account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to the moderator account metadata.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderator account was deactivated (soft delete). Null indicates active account.

models.name: discussion_board_moderator_sessions
models.description:
Authentication sessions for moderators with elevated access privileges.

Tracks active and expired sessions for moderator accounts, enabling audit tracing of moderator authentication events and connection contexts. Each session is associated with a single moderator and captures IP address, connection URL, and referrer information.

Sessions are managed automatically by the identity system and are not directly created or manipulated by users. They serve as operational logs for security monitoring and compliance tracking, with expired sessions automatically cleaned up by system processes.

No personal authentication data is stored here; moderator identity is referenced via the foreign key to the moderator table.

foreignFields.name: moderator_id
foreignFields.description: The moderator account this session belongs to. {@link discussion_board_moderator.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the session was initiated.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: The URL of the connection endpoint (e.g., the page or API route accessed).

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: The referrer URL that led to this session.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expired. Null indicates an active session.

models.name: discussion_board_articles
models.description:
Core article entities with title, content, publication status, and metadata.

Represents user-submitted content on the discussion board platform. Each article contains a title, body text, and associated metadata including category assignment and publication status.

Articles are created by citizens and can be moderated by administrators. The system tracks creation and modification timestamps for audit purposes. Soft deletion is supported to maintain historical integrity while allowing content removal according to moderation decisions.

Articles have a many-to-one relationship with categories and a one-to-one relationship with their current status. Article content is separate from attachments (images and files) which are managed through dedicated tables.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: Author's {@link discussion_board_citizen.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_categories_id
foreignFields.description: Assigned category {@link discussion_board_article_categories.id}. May be null if article is uncategorized.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Article title, limited to 200 characters. Should be concise but descriptive of content.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Main content of the article in Markdown format. Can contain paragraphs, lists, and basic formatting.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was created and first published. Set once at creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last modification to the article. Updated whenever title or body is changed.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was logically deleted. If null, the article is active. Used for soft delete functionality.

models.name: discussion_board_article_images
models.description:
Image attachments linked to articles with metadata for storage and rendering.

Stores metadata for images uploaded as attachments to articles, including dimensions, file type, size, and CDN paths for delivery. These attachments are managed entirely through their parent articles and do not have independent user interactions.

Each image has exactly one associated article and is referenced by unique file paths for retrieval. The system preserves original files and generates thumbnails for display efficiency while maintaining the original source for archival purposes. No modifications occur to uploaded images after initial storage.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Parent article this image is attached to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

plainFields.name: width
plainFields.description: Width of the image in pixels.

plainFields.name: height
plainFields.description: Height of the image in pixels.

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the image file (e.g., image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp).

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: File size of the image in bytes (maximum 5MB as per business rules).

plainFields.name: uploaded_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when the image was uploaded to the system.

plainFields.name: file_path
plainFields.description: Absolute URL path to the original image file in the cloud storage system.

plainFields.name: thumbnail_path
plainFields.description: Absolute URL path to the thumbnail version of the image in the cloud storage system.

models.name: discussion_board_article_files
models.description:
Stores file attachments linked to articles with metadata for download and integrity verification.

Each file attachment is associated with exactly one article through a foreign key relationship. These files are uploaded by citizens when creating articles and are managed exclusively through the article's lifecycle - citizens do not create, search, or manage these files independently. The actual storage metadata (location, MIME type, file size, SHA-256 hash) is referenced from the system-wide discussion_board_attachments table to avoid duplication and ensure consistency.

This table exists solely to establish the relationship between articles and their associated non-image file attachments. File access and retrieval occur through the article context. Soft deletion is supported to maintain audit trails while allowing for moderation actions that remove attachments from articles.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the article this file is attached to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_attachment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the master attachment metadata in Systematic component. {@link discussion_board_attachments.id}.

plainFields.name: file_name
plainFields.description: Original filename as uploaded by the user. May include extension.

plainFields.name: uploaded_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the file was uploaded and associated with the article.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Optional soft delete timestamp. When set, the file is no longer accessible through the article but remains in audit trail.

models.name: discussion_board_article_publication_log
models.description:
Historical audit trail of all publication status transitions for articles.

Records every state change in an article's lifecycle: draft -> pending -> published -> hidden -> deleted. Each record captures the exact moment a status transition occurred, who performed the action, and the before/after status values. This table is append-only and serves as the authoritative audit trail for compliance and moderation review.

Used by moderators to trace the history of content decisions, by analysts to study platform moderation patterns, and by compliance systems to satisfy regulatory requirements for content retention and change tracking. This table is never modified after creation. User actions trigger new records but never update existing ones.

foreignFields.name: article_id
foreignFields.description: The article whose status changed. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: moderation_actor_id
foreignFields.description: The moderator or citizen who performed the status change. {@link discussion_board_moderator.id}.

plainFields.name: status_from
plainFields.description: The publication state before the transition. Valid values: draft, pending, published, hidden, deleted.

plainFields.name: status_to
plainFields.description: The publication state after the transition. Valid values: draft, pending, published, hidden, deleted.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the status transition occurred. Immutable record creation time.

models.name: discussion_board_article_reports
models.description:
Records user reports submitted against articles, including reason, timestamp, and anonymous reporter ID.

This table captures citizen-initiated reports of problematic content. Each report is linked to a specific article and the reporting citizen, providing a traceable record for moderator review.

Reports support soft deletion to maintain audit trails while allowing users to withdraw or correct their submissions. Moderators can use this table to identify patterns of abuse and prioritize content review.

The report reason field is indexed for full-text search, allowing moderators to quickly find reports mentioning specific violations (e.g., "hate speech", "spam").

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Target article being reported. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: Citizen who submitted the report. {@link discussion_board_citizen.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: User-provided reason for the report, describing the violation (e.g., "hate speech", "spam", "inaccurate information"). Max 500 characters.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the report was submitted by the citizen.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp if the report was withdrawn by the citizen or deleted by moderator.

models.name: discussion_board_article_categories
models.description:
Manages category assignments for articles to enable content organization and filtering.

This table defines the taxonomy of categories that articles can be grouped under, such as "Politics", "Economics", "Technology". Categories are pre-defined by system administrators and assigned to articles during creation to facilitate efficient content discovery and navigation.

Users do not create or manage categories directly - they are static reference data that are referenced by articles. The category name serves as the primary business identifier for content classification and is used in filtering and search operations.

This is a subsidiary table that supports the article publishing workflow through relationships with discussion_board_articles, without requiring independent CRUD operations by end users.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: The unique category name used for content organization and filtering. Examples: "Politics", "Economics", "Technology". This field serves as the primary business identifier for the category.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the category was created in the system. Used for audit purposes and system administration.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the category name was last modified. Used for audit purposes and system administration.

models.name: discussion_board_article_comments
models.description:
User comments on articles with threaded replies and citizen authorship.

Stores individual comments submitted by citizens on articles, supporting up to 5 levels of threaded replies. Each comment is linked to a specific article and authored by a citizen. Comments can be replied to, and replies can themselves have replies up to the maximum depth limit.

Comments are managed independently of articles - citizens can search, edit, delete, or moderate comments without navigating through their parent articles. This table enables critical features like "Find all my comments" and "Show all comments on this topic across articles." Soft deletion preserves audit history while allowing content moderation.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the article this comment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the citizen who authored this comment. {@link discussion_board_citizen.id}.

foreignFields.name: parent_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent comment this is replying to, for threaded discussions. {@link discussion_board_article_comments.id}. Self-referential relationship for comment threads.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: The text content of the comment. Must contain user-submitted text for the article discussion.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was created. Required for audit and ordering.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was last updated. Required for tracking edits.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. When set, the comment is hidden from normal views but preserved in audit history.

models.name: discussion_board_article_status_logs
models.description:
Tracks all publication status transitions for articles including timestamp, actor, and new status (draft, pending, published, hidden, deleted).

This snapshot table maintains an audit trail of every status change throughout an article's lifecycle. Each record captures the moment an article's publication state was modified, who made the change, and the resulting status value.

The table is append-only - records are never updated or deleted, preserving historical accuracy for compliance and operational review. It references the main article entity to associate status transitions with specific content and records the actor (citizen or moderator) responsible for each transition.

foreignFields.name: article_id
foreignFields.description: References the article being monitored. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: actor_id
foreignFields.description: References the citizen or moderator who initiated the status change. {@link discussion_board_citizen.id}.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: The new publication status assigned to the article. Valid values: 'draft', 'pending', 'published', 'hidden', 'deleted'. Represents the state after the transition.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Optional reason provided for status change (e.g., 'Inappropriate content', 'Correction needed', 'System auto-approve').

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this status transition record was created. This reflects the exact moment the status changed.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this record was last updated. Will always equal created_at since this table is append-only and never modified after creation.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. May be set for compliance or audit archiving purposes, but records are retained in the system.

models.name: discussion_board_article_statuses
models.description:
Current publication status of articles with timestamp and audit context (draft, pending, published, hidden, deleted).

Tracks the authoritative current state of each article in its publication lifecycle. This table is not a history log but the single source of truth for an article's status at any given moment.

Each article can have only one active status record, creating a 1:1 relationship with discussion_board_articles. The status transitions occur when moderators approve, hide, or delete articles, and this table reflects the latest state.

The status field uses string enumeration for clarity, and the updated_at field captures when the status last changed. The deleted_at field enables soft deletion while maintaining auditability.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the article whose status is being tracked. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current publication status of the article. Valid values: draft, pending, published, hidden, deleted.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this status record was first created. Used for audit trail.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this status was last updated. Reflects the time of the last status transition.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. If null, status is active. If set, this status record is considered deleted.

models.name: discussion_board_comments
models.description:
Main comment entities linked to articles, storing content, author, and timestamps.

Stores user-generated comments on discussion board articles. Each comment is associated with a specific article and created by an authenticated citizen through their active session.

Comments remain attached to the article even if the article content changes, providing historical context. Citizens can post multiple comments per article, and each comment can receive replies and votes.

The comment content includes title and body fields for structured input formatting. Soft deletion is supported to maintain audit trails while allowing content moderation.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_post_id
foreignFields.description: The article this comment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_posts.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen who created this comment. {@link discussion_board_citizen.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Short summary or subject of the comment. Used as the comment header and in notification messages.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Full text content of the comment. Supports markdown formatting for rich text input.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was initially posted. Used for feed ordering and audit trails.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was last edited or modified. If never edited, equals created_at.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was soft-deleted. If null, the comment is active. Used for moderation and content recovery.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_replies
models.description:
Nested reply relationships for comments, enabling up to 5 levels of threading.

Stores comment replies that are attached to parent comments in a hierarchical structure. Each reply is associated with a specific parent comment and authored by a citizen. Replies can form threads of up to 5 levels deep as required by the commenting system.

The reply content is stored as a string field with full text search capability. Replies inherit the moderation context of their parent comment but do not have independent moderation permissions. Users can only create replies in the context of viewing a parent comment, and replies cannot exist without a parent.

When a parent comment is deleted, the replies are soft-deleted with it, maintaining data integrity. Replies are only accessible via the parent comment endpoint and are never exposed as independent resources in the API.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Parent comment that this reply belongs to. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: Citizen who authored this reply. {@link discussion_board_citizen.id}.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: The text content of the comment reply. Must contain the user-submitted reply text without HTML formatting.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this reply was created. Automatically set by system on creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this reply was last updated. Updated automatically when content is modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Indicates when this reply was removed by moderation or system. If null, reply is active.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_reports
models.description:
User reports on comments with reasons and timestamps for moderation tracking.

Records instances where citizens report comments for potential policy violations. Each report contains a reason code and timestamp, and is associated with the reported comment and the anonymous reporter's session.

Reports are processed by moderators through the comment moderation workflow and do not have independent existence outside of the comment moderation system. This table provides the audit trail for moderation actions and helps identify patterns of abuse without revealing reporter identity.

All reports are subject to soft deletion for compliance and audit purposes.

foreignFields.name: comment_id
foreignFields.description: The comment that was reported. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The reason code for the report (e.g., spam, harassment, misinformation). Standardized codes are defined in system configuration.

plainFields.name: reporter_session_id
plainFields.description: The session ID of the anonymous reporter. Cannot be linked to a specific citizen account to protect reporter privacy.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the report was submitted. Required for audit trail compliance.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the report was last updated (e.g., status change by moderator).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp for audit trail compliance. If null, the report is active.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_votes
models.description:
Tracks user upvotes and downvotes on discussion board comments.

Each vote represents a citizen's preference for a specific comment, either as a positive upvote or negative downvote. Users can change their vote at any time, and the system tracks the history through created_at and updated_at timestamps.

This table enables features such as comment popularity ranking, user reputation calculation, and moderation decisions based on community feedback. Each citizen can cast exactly one vote per comment, enforced by a unique constraint on the citizen_id and comment_id combination.

Votes are soft-deletable to maintain audit trails, with deleted_at tracking when a vote was removed (typically by moderation or user revocation).

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: The comment being voted on. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen who cast the vote. {@link discussion_board_citizen.id}.

plainFields.name: vote_type
plainFields.description: The type of vote: 'upvote' or 'downvote'. Represents the citizen's sentiment toward the comment.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the vote was first cast. Immutable after creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the vote was last modified (e.g., changed from upvote to downvote).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the vote was soft-deleted (e.g., by moderation or user revocation). Indicates the vote is no longer active.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_mod_actions
models.description:
Audit trail of moderator actions taken on comments for compliance and accountability.

Records all actions performed by moderators on comments including approve, hide, or warn actions. This table serves as a legal audit trail documenting the moderation workflow for regulatory compliance and dispute resolution.

Each record is tied to a specific comment and the moderator who performed the action. No user-initiated operations can modify this table - it is created systemically when moderators execute actions through approved interfaces. Deleted records are preserved with soft delete to maintain complete audit history.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: The comment that was acted upon. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: The moderator who performed the action. {@link discussion_board_moderator.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_moderation_action_type_id
foreignFields.description: The category and nature of the moderator action taken. References the moderation action type definition. {@link discussion_board_moderation_actions.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this moderation action was recorded. Indicates when the moderator executed the action.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to this moderation action record. This helps track any edits to the audit entry itself (rare).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp for compliance with data retention policies. Record remains in system for audit purposes.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_notifications
models.description:
Notification records for comment replies and @mentions, tied to user recipients.

Automatically generated system notifications triggered when a user receives a reply to their comment or is mentioned in a comment thread. These notifications are tracked for user engagement metrics and user interface rendering in notification centers without requiring direct user management.

Each notification links to the recipient user and the source comment that triggered the notification. Notifications are immutable after creation and are typically cleared when viewed by the user, but remain in system records for analytics and audit purposes.

The type field identifies the notification category (reply or mention), and the metadata field stores additional context such as thread depth or mentioned username.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: The recipient user who receives this notification. {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: The comment that triggered this notification (e.g., a reply or mention). {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: Type of notification event. Valid values: "reply" (user replied to their comment) or "mention" (user was mentioned in comment).

plainFields.name: metadata
plainFields.description: Additional JSON-formatted context about the notification, such as {"mentionedUsername":"john_doe", "threadDepth":2}. Used for UI rendering and analytics.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this notification was generated and queued for delivery. Never updated after creation.

models.name: discussion_board_attachment_images
models.description:
Stores image attachments for posts with metadata including file size, dimensions, MIME type, and upload timestamp.

Contains all metadata for images uploaded by citizens to articles. This table tracks the physical attributes and integrity of image files while maintaining association with both the article they belong to and the citizen who uploaded them.

Each image entry represents a single file upload with precise technical specifications: file size in bytes, dimensions in pixels, MIME type for content validation, and SHA-256 hash for content integrity verification. All images are stored with temporary storage paths before CDN integration.

Soft deletion is supported to maintain audit trails while allowing content moderation. The created_at and updated_at timestamps ensure accurate tracking of the image lifecycle. The system uses this table to enforce attachment limits (5 images per post) and image quality constraints (max 5MB, JPG/PNG/WebP formats).

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: The article this image is attached to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen who uploaded this image. {@link discussion_board_citizen.id}.

plainFields.name: filename
plainFields.description: Original filename of the uploaded image file.

plainFields.name: filesize
plainFields.description: Size of the image file in bytes. Must not exceed 5MB (5242880 bytes) as per business rules.

plainFields.name: width
plainFields.description: Image width in pixels as determined by metadata extraction.

plainFields.name: height
plainFields.description: Image height in pixels as determined by metadata extraction.

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the image file. Only allows: 'image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/webp' as specified in business rules.

plainFields.name: sha256_hash
plainFields.description: SHA-256 cryptographic hash of the file content for integrity verification and duplicate detection.

plainFields.name: storage_path
plainFields.description: Temporary storage path for the image file before CDN integration.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the image was uploaded. Required for all business entities.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the image metadata was last updated. Required for all business entities.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the image was soft-deleted. Allows for content moderation and retrieval.

models.name: discussion_board_attachment_files
models.description:
Non-image file attachments for articles including PDFs, documents, spreadsheets, and archives.

Stores all non-image file attachments that users can upload with their posts. Each file is identified by its SHA-256 hash for content integrity, with filename, size (in bytes), and MIME type metadata for proper handling and security validation.

Files are linked to specific posts through foreign key relationship and are managed exclusively through their parent post operations. Uploads are restricted to specific formats (PDF, DOCX, TXT, CSV, ZIP) and maximum size of 10MB as specified in business rules.

The system tracks full metadata including creation and update timestamps for audit purposes and implements soft deletion to preserve historical context during content moderation.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_post_id
foreignFields.description: The article this file is attached to. {@link discussion_board_posts.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: The user who uploaded this file. {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

plainFields.name: filename
plainFields.description: Original filename of the uploaded file including extension. Example: "annual_report.pdf".

plainFields.name: size_bytes
plainFields.description: File size in bytes (must not exceed 10MB = 10,485,760 bytes as per business rules).

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the file (e.g., application/pdf, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document). Must be one of: application/pdf, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, text/plain, text/csv, application/zip for compliance with specified file types.

plainFields.name: sha256_hash
plainFields.description: SHA-256 hash of the file content. Used for content integrity verification and duplicate detection. Format is 64-character hexadecimal string.

plainFields.name: storage_path
plainFields.description: Path where the file is stored in the CDN or storage system. Format: /attachments/files/{sha256_hash}/{filename} to ensure uniqueness and avoid collisions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this file was first uploaded. Required for audit trail and tracking upload history.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this file's metadata was last updated. Used to track modifications to attachments.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Optional timestamp for soft deletion. When set, indicates the file has been logically removed but preserved in the database for audit purposes. Null means file is still active.

models.name: discussion_board_reports
models.description:
Records all user reports on posts and comments including reason, timestamp, and anonymous reporter ID.

Tracks violations reported by citizens or moderators against platform content (articles, comments). Each report contains the reporting actor's identifier, the targeted content identifier, and a detailed reason for the violation. Reports remain in system regardless of target content being deleted, preserving audit trail for compliance and moderation reviews.

Supports both citizen and moderator reporting. The system does not store the report content itself but captures the reason and context. Reports are processed by moderation team through independent workflows.

foreignFields.name: reporter_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen who submitted this report. {@link discussion_board_citizen.id}. Nullable because moderators can also report content.

foreignFields.name: moderator_reporter_id
foreignFields.description: The moderator who submitted this report. {@link discussion_board_moderator.id}. Nullable because citizens can also report content.

plainFields.name: target_type
plainFields.description: Type of content being reported. Valid values: 'article', 'comment'. Required to identify the target context for the report.

plainFields.name: target_id
plainFields.description: ID of the content being reported. References either discussion_board_articles.id or discussion_board_comments.id depending on target_type. Required for linking report to specific content.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The reason provided for the report. User-entered text describing why the content was reported. Must include sufficient detail for moderation review.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the report was submitted. Always recorded and cannot be null.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the report was last updated. Tracks when moderation actions modify the report status.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. If set, indicates this report has been archived for compliance or resolution. Records when the report was removed from active queue.

plainFields.name: report_state
plainFields.description: Current state of the report. Valid values: 'pending', 'reviewed', 'dismissed', 'action_taken'. Tracks moderation workflow status for reporting system.

models.name: discussion_board_moderation_actions
models.description:
Records every moderator action (dismiss, remove, warn) with reason, timestamp, moderator ID, and target content ID.

Tracks all actions taken by moderators on reported content such as posts, comments, or user accounts. Each action is logged with a specific type (dismiss, remove, warn), reason for the action, the moderator who performed it, and the target entity that was acted upon. This table serves as the primary audit trail for moderation activities across the entire platform.

Actions can be viewed independently by moderators for review, analytics, and performance evaluation. The target entity can be any content type (discussion_board_posts, discussion_board_comments, etc.) using a generic target_id with target_type discrimination. Soft delete capability allows for moderation reversal with full historical preservation.

foreignFields.name: moderator_id
foreignFields.description: The moderator who performed this moderation action. {@link discussion_board_moderator.id}.

foreignFields.name: report_id
foreignFields.description: The user report that triggered this moderation action, if any. {@link discussion_board_reports.id}.

foreignFields.name: target_id
foreignFields.description: Generic ID of the target entity (post, comment, user, etc.) that was moderated. {@link discussion_board_posts.id} or other relevant entity if target_type matches.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of moderation action taken. Valid values: 'dismiss', 'remove', 'warn', 'suspend', 'ban'. Represents the specific action performed by the moderator.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Detailed reason for the moderation action, including policy violation specifics. Required for transparency and appeal review.

plainFields.name: target_type
plainFields.description: Type of the target entity being moderated. Valid values: 'post', 'comment', 'user', 'account', 'attachment'. Indicates what kind of content was acted upon.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderation action was performed. Tracks exact moment of moderator decision.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderation action record was last updated. Tracks changes to action details like reason revision.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this moderation action was logically deleted (soft delete). Null if action is still active. Preserves audit trail even when reversed.

models.name: discussion_board_warnings
models.description:
Tracks user warnings for policy violations, including count, date, severity level, and moderator-provided reason.

Used by moderators to document and track violations committed by citizens. Each warning is associated with a specific citizen and records the severity level (e.g., low, medium, high) and a justification from the moderator. Warnings contribute to reputation scores and suspension decisions.

Warnings remain active until expiring or being lifted through appeal. Multiple warnings can exist for one citizen, but only one active warning per citizen at a time. Deleted warnings preserve audit history for compliance purposes.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen who received this warning. {@link discussion_board_citizen.id}.

plainFields.name: warning_count
plainFields.description: Cumulative warning count for this citizen at time of issuing. Used to determine escalation thresholds for suspensions.

plainFields.name: severity
plainFields.description: Severity level of the warning. Values are: low, medium, high. Determines impact on reputation score and suspension eligibility.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Moderator-provided explanation for issuing this warning. Must include specific policy violation reference.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this warning was issued by the moderator.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this warning was last updated (e.g., edited by moderator).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this warning was administratively removed. Soft delete preserves audit trail.

models.name: discussion_board_suspensions
models.description:
Manages temporary account suspensions for policy violations with defined start and end dates.

Tracks periods during which citizens are temporarily restricted from platform access due to moderation decisions. Suspensions are initiated by moderators and maintain audit trails through temporal fields. Each suspension is linked to a specific citizen and includes a reason for the action, as well as the status of any related appeals. The system supports resumption of access through the unsuspended_at field, which may be null if the suspension is still active or indefinite.

Suspensions are managed entirely through the moderation workflow and have no direct interaction or management by citizens. This ensures that access restrictions follow proper bureaucratic procedures and are not bypassed by users. All suspension records are preserved for compliance and audit purposes, even after suspension periods end.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen whose account has been suspended. {@link discussion_board_citizen.id}.

plainFields.name: suspended_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the suspension took effect. Always set when a suspension is applied by a moderator.

plainFields.name: unsuspended_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the suspension ends and access is restored. If null, the suspension is still active or indefinite.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Detailed explanation of the policy violation that led to the suspension. Must be specific enough for audit trail purposes.

plainFields.name: appeal_status
plainFields.description: Current status of any appeal against this suspension. Valid values: pending, approved, denied. Used to track user appeals and resolution pathways.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the suspension record was created in the system. Immutable.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the suspension record was last modified (e.g., appeal status changed).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete marker. When set, indicates the suspension record has been logically removed but retained for audit purposes.

models.name: discussion_board_bans
models.description:
Permanent account bans as a final moderation action.

Records permanent removals of citizens from the discussion board as a consequence of policy violations. Each ban represents a final moderation decision that is immutable unless formally appealed and overturned through the appeals process.

Bans are created by moderators based on accumulated violations, serious misconduct, or repeated policy breaches. The ban record includes the justification for the decision, the initiating moderator, and the target citizen account.

Bans may eventually be appealed through the discussion_board_appeals table, but the ban record itself remains as a permanent audit trail.

Soft deletion is supported to maintain data integrity while allowing for potential reversal in exceptional circumstances.

foreignFields.name: moderator_id
foreignFields.description: The moderator who issued the permanent ban. {@link discussion_board_moderator.id}.

foreignFields.name: citizen_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen account that was permanently banned. {@link discussion_board_citizen.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the permanent ban was issued by the moderator.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the ban record was last modified (e.g., when appeal status changed).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp for audit trail maintenance. Null means ban is active - non-null indicates ban has been lifted or reversed.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current state of the ban. Valid values: 'active', 'appealed', 'lifted'. Indicates whether the ban is ongoing, under appeal, or has been reversed.

plainFields.name: justification
plainFields.description: Detailed explanation of why the permanent ban was issued. Must include specific policy violations, accumulated violations, or misconduct evidence that led to this final decision.

models.name: discussion_board_appeals
models.description:
Stores user appeals of moderation decisions with explanation text and final moderator resolution.

Allows citizens to formally appeal moderation actions taken against their content or accounts. Each appeal contains a detailed explanation of why the user believes the moderation decision was incorrect or unfair. Moderators review these appeals and issue resolutions with justification.

Appeals are independent entities with their own lifecycle: submitted by a citizen, reviewed by a moderator, and resolved with a final outcome. The system tracks the status of each appeal and preserves historical records for audit.

This table supports direct user-facing UI for submitting appeals and moderator workflows for handling them, requiring independent CRUD API endpoints.

foreignFields.name: reporter_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen who submitted the appeal. {@link discussion_board_citizen.id}.

foreignFields.name: target_id
foreignFields.description: The moderation report this appeal is addressing. {@link discussion_board_reports.id}.

foreignFields.name: moderator_id
foreignFields.description: The moderator who resolved this appeal. {@link discussion_board_moderator.id}. Null until resolved.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The user's explanation for why they are appealing the moderation decision. Must contain specific details about the perceived error or unfairness.

plainFields.name: resolution
plainFields.description: The moderator's formal resolution and justification for their final decision. Null until the appeal is resolved.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the appeal. Valid values: pending (awaiting moderator review), under_review (actively being reviewed), resolved (moderator made a decision), withdrawn (user withdrew the appeal).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the appeal was created. Always recorded when user submits the appeal.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the appeal was last modified (e.g., when status changed or resolution was added). Updated on every state transition.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Used for compliance and audit trail purposes. Null if appeal is active, set when formally deleted.

models.name: discussion_board_moderation_audit_trails
models.description:
Comprehensive audit log preserving complete original content, metadata, and moderation history for all removed or hidden items.

This snapshot table captures the exact state of content before moderation actions, providing a permanent compliance record of what existed before deletion, hiding, or modification. Used for legal compliance, dispute resolution, and auditing purposes. Records are append-only and cannot be modified after creation.

Each audit record links to a specific moderation action and preserves the complete state of the original content (title, body, attachments, metadata, timestamps) as it appeared prior to the moderation decision. This ensures transparency and accountability in platform governance.

foreignFields.name: moderation_action_id
foreignFields.description: The moderation action that triggered this audit record. {@link discussion_board_moderation_actions.id}.

foreignFields.name: post_id
foreignFields.description: The original post that was moderated, if applicable. {@link discussion_board_posts.id}.

foreignFields.name: comment_id
foreignFields.description: The original comment that was moderated, if applicable. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

foreignFields.name: report_id
foreignFields.description: The user report that initiated this moderation action, if applicable. {@link discussion_board_reports.id}.

plainFields.name: content_type
plainFields.description: The type of content being audited (e.g., "post", "comment", "profile"). Used for quick filtering and type-specific processing.

plainFields.name: content_id
plainFields.description: The original unique identifier of the content being audited (independent of foreign keys to allow referencing different content types).

plainFields.name: original_title
plainFields.description: The exact title of the content before moderation. Preserved for historical accuracy and context.

plainFields.name: original_body
plainFields.description: The complete original body text of the content before any moderation action. Preserved exactly as submitted by the user.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The exact timestamp when this audit record was created, capturing when the moderation decision was enacted.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete flag to maintain audit trail integrity while managing record lifecycle. If null, record is active and preserved.

plainFields.name: original_metadata
plainFields.description: JSON string containing original content metadata (tags, categories, attachment references, etc.) preserved in its original format.

plainFields.name: reason_for_modification
plainFields.description: The specific reason provided for the moderation action taken on this content. Includes policy violation details.

models.name: discussion_board_citizen_violations
models.description:
Tracks violation records for citizens, including moderation actions and counts for suspension decisions.

Records specific violations committed by citizens that trigger reputation penalties and potential suspensions. Each violation is tied to a specific moderation action taken by a moderator and represents a concrete policy breach.

Violations persist as audit records even when associated content is removed. This table enables reputation scoring algorithms by providing a comprehensive history of citizen misconduct. The data in this table is critical for automated suspension decisions and manual review workflows.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: Citizen who committed the violation. {@link discussion_board_citizen.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_moderation_action_id
foreignFields.description: Moderation action that resulted in this violation. {@link discussion_board_moderation_actions.id}.

plainFields.name: summary
plainFields.description: Concise summary of the violation reason, including the policy violated (e.g., "Spam advertising", "Harassment", "Illegal content").

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this violation record was created, matching the time of the moderation action.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this violation record was last updated, typically when additional context was added.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp to maintain audit trail while allowing moderation to 'hide' records when necessary.

models.name: discussion_board_citizen_trust_scores
models.description:
Cumulative trust score for citizens based on approved content and positive interaction history.

Represents the system's calculated trust level for each citizen, derived from the quality of their posts, comments, moderation history, and report responses. Higher scores indicate more reliable and constructive community members. The score is algorithmically updated based on peer feedback, content moderation outcomes, and community engagement patterns.

This table supports features like trusted-user badges, priority content visibility, and reduced moderation scrutiny. It is not directly editable by users but is updated automatically in response to community interactions.

Each citizen has exactly one trust score record, creating a 1:1 relationship with the citizen profile. The record is soft-deletable to maintain audit trails when citizen accounts are suspended or removed.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: Citizen profile this trust score belongs to. {@link discussion_board_citizen.id}.

plainFields.name: trusted_score
plainFields.description: Current trust score value, calculated as a weighted average based on post quality, comment reception, moderation history, and report outcomes. Higher values indicate greater community trust.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this trust score record was initially created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this trust score value.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this trust score was logically deleted (e.g., due to citizen account suspension or removal). Null indicates active record.

models.name: discussion_board_citizen_suspensions
models.description:
Historical records of temporary suspensions imposed on citizens for policy violations.
