Captures the complete history of account restrictions applied by moderators, providing an immutable audit trail for compliance and review. Each suspension represents a period during which a citizen's account was temporarily disabled due to accumulated violations or severe misconduct.

Suspension records are append-only and never modified after creation. The system uses these records to enforce access restrictions and determine eligibility for appeal or reinstatement. Querying this table allows moderators to analyze patterns of repeated behavior and assess the effectiveness of disciplinary actions.

This table is linked to the citizen entity via citizen_id, and each suspension has defined start and end timestamps to indicate the exact period of restriction.

foreignFields.name: citizen_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen who was suspended. {@link discussion_board_citizen.id}.

plainFields.name: suspension_start
plainFields.description: The exact date and time when the suspension took effect. This is the moment access was revoked.

plainFields.name: suspension_end
plainFields.description: The exact date and time when the suspension will expire and access will be restored. This may be in the future or may have already passed.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The specific reason for suspension as stated by the moderator. Must follow standardized reasons from moderation policy documentation (e.g., 'repeated violations', 'inflammatory content', 'impersonation').

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this suspension record was created in the system. Matches suspension_start in most cases.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last modification to this suspension record. Will be updated if the suspension was modified (e.g., extended) by a moderator.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. If set, the suspension record is logically deleted but preserved for audit purposes. Only system administrators can perform this.

models.name: discussion_board_moderator_actions
models.description:
Logs all moderation actions taken by moderators on content, user reports, or citizens.

Tracks every decision made by moderators including actions like dismissal, removal, warnings, suspensions, and bans. Each action is linked to a specific moderator, target entity (article, comment, report, or citizen), and includes the reason for the action. This table serves as the primary audit trail for moderation workflows and enables independent querying of moderation history by type, target, or moderator.

Moderators can search and filter actions across all content types, making this a core independent entity rather than a subsidiary of specific items. System reports and compliance audits rely on this table for visibility into moderation activities.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator who performed the action. {@link discussion_board_moderator.id}.

plainFields.name: target_type
plainFields.description:
Type of target entity being moderated. Valid values: article, comment, report, citizen. Used for polymorphic relationship.

Enforces business-rule validation to prevent invalid target values.

plainFields.name: target_id
plainFields.description:
ID of the target entity being moderated (article, comment, report, or citizen). Must correspond to target_type field.

For example, if target_type is 'article', target_id references discussion_board_articles.id.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Type of moderation action taken. Valid values: dismiss, remove, warn, suspend, ban, approve.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Detailed reason for the moderation action, including policy violation and context.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderation action was performed.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderation action was last updated (e.g., if edited).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the record was logically deleted (soft delete). Null if active.

models.name: discussion_board_report_aggregations
models.description:
Aggregates total reports per content item, triggering automated moderation when thresholds are exceeded.

System-generated aggregation that counts the total number of user reports submitted against each content item (article or comment). This table serves as the basis for automated moderation workflows - when report counts reach predefined thresholds, the system triggers review queues or automatic content actions.

The aggregation updates in real-time as new reports are submitted and older reports are resolved. Each row represents a single content item's aggregated report count, enabling efficient threshold checks without live joins across report tables. This is a purely operational table that is managed by system logic, not by direct user interaction.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the article being reported. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the comment being reported. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

plainFields.name: count
plainFields.description: Total number of reports aggregated for this content item. When this count reaches the system threshold (e.g., 5), automated moderation actions are triggered.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the aggregation record was first created. Records the initial moment the content item received its first report.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the report count was last updated. Updated every time a new report is added or an existing report is resolved.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this aggregation record was logically deleted. Supports soft deletion for data retention compliance and audit trail requirements, allowing historical tracking of report aggregation lifecycle.

models.name: discussion_board_notification_templates
models.description:
System-generated notification templates defining message content and metadata for alerts and communications.

Contains predefined message templates used by the notification system to inform users about system events, moderation actions, and platform updates. These templates are configured by administrators and referenced by notification_records to generate personalized messages.

Each template includes a title for identification and a content body that may contain placeholders for dynamic data (e.g., {username}, {post_title}). The trigger_event field specifies the system event that activates this template. Metadata can store additional configuration parameters such as priority level or communication channel preference.

Templates are versioned through soft deletion rather than historical snapshots, allowing administrators to disable outdated templates while preserving audit trail. Actual historical versions are not tracked in this table - only the current active state.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Human-readable title for this notification template, used for administrative identification and management.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: The actual message content of the notification, potentially containing placeholders for dynamic substitution (e.g., {username}, {post_title}) that are resolved at runtime.

plainFields.name: trigger_event
plainFields.description: The system event or condition that triggers this notification template to be dispatched (e.g., 'comment_reply', 'report_submitted', 'moderation_action').

plainFields.name: metadata
plainFields.description: JSON-formatted string containing additional configuration parameters for this template (e.g., priority level, channel preference, visibility rules).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this notification template was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this notification template was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this notification template was soft-deleted (null if active). Used for audit trail and template versioning without destroying historical reference.

models.name: discussion_board_notification_delivery_logs
models.description:
Tracks delivery status and history for system-generated notifications.

Records when each notification was attempted to be delivered to recipients, including success/failure outcomes and timestamps. Automatically generated by the system when notification_records are processed for delivery. This table provides audit trail for notification delivery reliability and performance metrics.

Used for monitoring delivery success rates, troubleshooting failed notifications, and ensuring compliance with communication requirements. Does not contain notification content itself but links to the associated notification_record for full context.

foreignFields.name: notification_record_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the notification event being tracked. {@link discussion_board_notification_records.id}.

plainFields.name: delivery_status
plainFields.description: Current delivery status: 'pending', 'delivered', or 'failed'. Indicates delivery state at time of recording.

plainFields.name: delivered_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when notification was successfully delivered to recipient. null if delivery failed or not yet attempted.

plainFields.name: failed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when notification delivery attempt failed. null if delivery was successful or not yet attempted.

plainFields.name: error_message
plainFields.description: Detailed error message explaining why delivery failed if delivery_status is 'failed'. Provide specific error details for debugging support.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this delivery log record was created. Represents when the system first attempted to deliver the notification.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this delivery log record was last updated. Updates when delivery_status changes or failed_at/error_message are added.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp for audit trail purposes. If null, record is still active; if set, the record is marked for archival.

models.name: discussion_board_notification_preferences
models.description:
User-specific settings that control notification delivery preferences across different communication channels.

Stores opt-in/opt-out preferences for each user regarding different notification types and delivery methods. Users can configure their preferences to receive notifications via email, push notifications, or in-app alerts for various system events.

The preferences are associated with either a citizen or moderator account (mutually exclusive), allowing personalized notification control based on user role.

This table supports user customization of notification behavior while maintaining data integrity through strict foreign key relationships with actor tables. All preference settings are timestamped for audit and compliance purposes.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the citizen user whose preferences are stored. {@link discussion_board_citizen.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the moderator user whose preferences are stored. {@link discussion_board_moderator.id}.

plainFields.name: email_enabled
plainFields.description: Whether email notifications are enabled for this user. True allows email delivery of notifications.

plainFields.name: push_enabled
plainFields.description: Whether push notifications are enabled for this user. True allows mobile app push alerts.

plainFields.name: in_app_enabled
plainFields.description: Whether in-app notifications are enabled for this user. True allows notifications within the web interface.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when these notification preferences were first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when these notification preferences were last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when these notification preferences were deleted (soft delete). Null indicates active preferences.

models.name: discussion_board_notification_read_status
models.description:
Tracks when users have read specific notifications, enabling read/unread indicators and notification management.

Records the read status of notifications for individual users. Each record represents a single user's read state for a specific notification event, automatically updated when the user views the notification.

Used to maintain notification visibility state across device sessions and provide UI indicators for unread notifications. The system automatically creates and updates these records without direct user interaction, ensuring accurate status tracking across all platforms.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_notification_record_id
foreignFields.description: The notification record this read status pertains to. {@link discussion_board_notification_records.id}.

plainFields.name: user_id
plainFields.description: The citizen or moderator user who has read the notification. References the actor's unique identifier in their respective table.

plainFields.name: read_at
plainFields.description: The exact timestamp when the user marked this notification as read. This is automatically set when the notification is viewed by the user.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this read status record was initially created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this read status record was last updated (e.g., when status changed or was reconfirmed).

models.name: discussion_board_notification_records
models.description:
Records notification events triggered by user actions such as replies, reports, moderator actions, and appeal outcomes.

Captures business-critical notifications that users receive when their content is interacted with or modified by others. These events must be independently managed by users in a notification center UI, enabling filtering by type (e.g., 'all moderator actions affecting me') and marking as read/unread regardless of the source entity.

The notification event is decoupled from its source (post, comment, etc.), allowing independent lifecycle management without affecting the original content. Each record points to a specific recipient (user) and has a type defining the triggering action, with targeted foreign keys to ensure referential integrity to the triggering entity.

Soft delete is supported to allow users to clear notification history while preserving audit trail for compliance.

foreignFields.name: recipient_id
foreignFields.description: The user who receives this notification. {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

foreignFields.name: target_post_id
foreignFields.description: The post that triggered this notification (e.g., reply to post). {@link discussion_board_posts.id}.

foreignFields.name: target_comment_id
foreignFields.description: The comment that triggered this notification (e.g., reply to comment). {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

foreignFields.name: target_report_id
foreignFields.description: The report on content that triggered this notification (e.g., report processed). {@link discussion_board_reports.id}.

foreignFields.name: target_moderation_action_id
foreignFields.description: The moderation action that triggered this notification (e.g., post hidden). {@link discussion_board_moderation_actions.id}.

foreignFields.name: target_appeal_id
foreignFields.description: The appeal that triggered this notification (e.g., appeal resolved). {@link discussion_board_appeals.id}.

plainFields.name: notification_type
plainFields.description: Type of notification event. Valid values: 'comment_reply', 'post_report', 'moderation_action', 'appeal_outcome'. Indicates the business action that triggered this notification.

plainFields.name: metadata
plainFields.description: JSON-encoded additional context or data specific to the notification type. May include sender ID, reason, action details, or custom metadata. Use only for variable data that doesn't warrant dedicated fields.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the notification event was created and queued for delivery.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to this notification record (e.g., when marked as read).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this notification was soft-deleted by the recipient. Null if still active.

plainFields.name: is_read
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the recipient has viewed this notification. False when created, true when marked as read in the notification center.

models.name: discussion_board_audit_events
models.description:
Tracks all system-level audit events including user actions, moderation decisions, and system state changes.

Records comprehensive audit trail of activities across the entire system, providing security, compliance, and operational monitoring capabilities. Each audit event captures the action performed, the actor responsible, the target entity affected, and the precise timestamp of occurrence.

This table supports critical functions such as security investigations, regulatory compliance reporting, system behavior analysis, and troubleshooting of system anomalies. The audit trail enables forensic analysis of system operations and ensures accountability for all system modifications and user actions.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen who performed the action, if applicable. {@link discussion_board_citizen.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: The moderator who performed the action, if applicable. {@link discussion_board_moderator.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: The article affected by this audit event, if applicable. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: The comment affected by this audit event, if applicable. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_attachment_file_id
foreignFields.description: The file attachment affected by this audit event, if applicable. {@link discussion_board_attachment_files.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_attachment_image_id
foreignFields.description: The image attachment affected by this audit event, if applicable. {@link discussion_board_attachment_images.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_channel_id
foreignFields.description: The channel affected by this audit event, if applicable. {@link discussion_board_channels.id}.

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: Classification of the audit event type. Valid values: user_action, moderation_action, system_state_change, security_event, compliance_event. Defines category of operation performed.

plainFields.name: action
plainFields.description: Specific action performed. Examples: post_created, comment_deleted, article_hidden, user_login, configuration_changed, file_uploaded. Describes the exact operation executed.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the audit event including context, parameters, and additional metadata. May include JSON-encoded structured data for complex events.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: The IP address from which the action originated, if available for traceability and security analysis.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: The user agent string of the client device that generated the event, useful for identifying platform and browser context.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the audit event was recorded in the system. Never null as every event must be logged at time of occurrence.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last modification to this audit record, if any. Useful for timestamp consistency verification.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete marker indicating when this audit record was marked for deletion. Maintains compliance audit trail while allowing logical removal.

models.name: discussion_board_security_logs
models.description:
Records security-related events including authentication attempts, IP changes, and access violations.

Tracks system security events for compliance and threat detection. Each record captures the exact time, origin (IP), and context of a security-relevant system event. These logs are immutable and are used for forensic analysis, intrusion detection, and regulatory auditing.

Event types include failed authentication attempts, suspicious login patterns, privilege escalation attempts, and configuration changes that impact system security. The logs preserve original context for security investigations and serve as the primary audit trail for security operations.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: The user who triggered the security event. {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: Type of security event (e.g., 'failed_login', 'ip_change', 'privilege_escalation'). Standardized values for consistent categorization.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the security event originated. Used for geo-location and threat analysis.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL endpoint or system path where the security event occurred. Useful for identifying affected system components.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed text description of the security event, including contextual information and system-generated messages.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the security event was recorded in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the security log entry was last updated. Typically same as created_at for immutable records.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this security log entry was logically deleted. Always null for audit compliance - retained indefinitely for forensic purposes.

models.name: discussion_board_operational_logs
models.description:
Captures system performance metrics, error events, and operational diagnostics for monitoring and troubleshooting.

Records critical system events including service failures, resource exhaustion, timeout thresholds, and internal processing errors. These logs are essential for monitoring system health, identifying performance bottlenecks, and supporting incident response.

Each entry represents a discrete operational event with context about which system component triggered the event, the severity level, and any associated error codes or diagnostic metadata. The logs are append-only and never modified after creation to preserve integrity for compliance and debugging purposes.

Applications use these logs to trigger alerts, generate system health reports, and analyze failure patterns over time.

Refer to discussion_board_audit_events for user-facing audit events and discussion_board_security_logs for authentication-related events.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the operational event occurred. Immutable timestamp of system event.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When the log entry was written. Always equal to created_at since logs are immutable.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for soft deletion in compliance with data retention policies.

plainFields.name: component
plainFields.description: System component that generated the log event (e.g., "auth-service", "notification-queue", "search-engine").

plainFields.name: severity
plainFields.description: Severity level of the event: "info", "warning", "error", "critical".

plainFields.name: error_code
plainFields.description: System-specific error code for machine processing (e.g., "DB_TIMEOUT", "QUEUE_FULL").

plainFields.name: message
plainFields.description: Human-readable description of the operational event and context.

plainFields.name: metadata
plainFields.description: JSON string containing additional diagnostic details such as stack traces, process IDs, or system metrics.

models.name: discussion_board_compliance_records
models.description:
Stores legally required audit trails including moderation decisions with timestamps and reason codes for regulatory compliance.

This snapshot table captures immutable records of compliance-related events for regulatory auditing and legal investigations. Each record stores the action performed, the reason code, original data snapshot, and references to both the actor who performed the action and the affected content entity.

The table follows an append-only pattern - records are never modified or deleted, ensuring data integrity for compliance purposes. Records are referenced by external audit systems and are subject to retention policies governed by regulatory requirements.

This table serves as the primary audit trail source for compliance verification, enabling reconstruction of historical events with full context including the original state of content before moderation actions.

foreignFields.name: moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator who performed the compliance action. {@link discussion_board_moderator.id}.

foreignFields.name: citizen_id
foreignFields.description: Citizen who performed or was affected by the compliance action. {@link discussion_board_citizen.id}.

foreignFields.name: article_id
foreignFields.description: Article affected by the compliance action. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: comment_id
foreignFields.description: Comment affected by the compliance action. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

foreignFields.name: report_id
foreignFields.description: User report that triggered the compliance action. {@link discussion_board_reports.id}.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of compliance action performed (e.g., 'content_removed', 'account_suspended', 'warning_issued'). Must be a predefined system value from compliance policy.

plainFields.name: reason_code
plainFields.description: Standardized compliance reason code (e.g., 'POL-001', 'HAR-005', 'SPM-002') from regulatory policy documentation. Used for audit categorization and reporting.

plainFields.name: original_data
plainFields.description: JSON string representation of the content state at time of action, including full text, metadata, and attachments. Used for forensic reconstruction during compliance audits.

plainFields.name: content_type
plainFields.description: Type of content affected by this action (e.g., 'article', 'comment', 'report'). Used for routing and filtering compliance events.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the compliance event was recorded. This is immutable and represents the point-in-time of the action.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this record was last updated. For compliance tables, this typically mirrors created_at since records are immutable.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of actor who performed the action ('moderator' or 'citizen'). Used for indexing and filtering audit events by actor role.
